questions.question: Describe circuit training and explain two advantages and two disadvantages.
questions.correctAnswer: Circuit training involves performing a series of exercises at different stations, one after another, with a short rest between stations. Advantages: targets multiple fitness components; reduces tedium through variety. Disadvantages: requires equipment and space; may not develop one specific component enough for elite performers.

questions.question: What is Fartlek training and which two energy systems does it develop?
questions.correctAnswer: Fartlek training ("speed play") is a form of continuous training where the intensity varies - alternating between fast and slow running over varied terrain. It develops both the aerobic system (during slower sections) and the anaerobic system (during sprints and high-intensity bursts).

questions.question: Explain the difference between continuous training and interval training.
questions.correctAnswer: Continuous training involves exercising at a steady, moderate intensity for a sustained period without rest (e.g. a 30-minute jog at 70% max HR). Interval training alternates periods of high-intensity exercise with periods of rest or low-intensity recovery (e.g. 8 × 400m sprints with 2-minute recovery). Continuous is purely aerobic; interval develops both aerobic and anaerobic fitness.

questions.question: Which training method is most appropriate for developing power? Explain why.
questions.correctAnswer: Plyometric training is most appropriate for developing power. It uses the stretch-shortening cycle of muscles, where a rapid eccentric stretch is followed immediately by an explosive concentric contraction. This develops the ability to produce maximal force in the shortest time (power = strength × speed). Examples include box jumps and depth jumps.

questions.question: A footballer wants to improve their cardiovascular endurance. Which two training methods would you recommend and why?
questions.correctAnswer: Fartlek training and interval training. Fartlek replicates the variable pace of football (jogging, sprinting, walking) and develops both aerobic and anaerobic fitness. Interval training with short, high-intensity bursts and recovery periods mimics the intermittent nature of football and improves both cardiovascular endurance and the ability to recover quickly between efforts.

questions.question: Describe plyometric training and explain why it carries a high risk of injury.
questions.correctAnswer: Plyometric training involves rapid, powerful movements using the stretch-shortening cycle (e.g. box jumps, depth jumps, bounding). It carries a high risk of injury because the explosive movements place enormous stress on joints (especially knees and ankles) and the eccentric loading on muscles can cause micro-tears. It requires a foundation of strength and good technique to perform safely.
